name: kama
comment: Hand-maintained TextMate grammar. Two guards keep it honest and BOTH are load-bearing: tools/check-syntax-drift.sh greps kama.l's keyword + numeric-suffix tables (it can see that a rule EXISTS), and tools/check-syntax.sh runs the real vscode-textmate engine over tests/syntax/ (it can see that a rule FIRES). The second one exists because the first cannot catch a rule that is present, correct, and unreachable — see the ordering note on `patterns` below.

comments.comment: `/*` does NOT nest in kama.l either (a single IN_COMMENT state, popped by the first `*/`), so the non-nesting rule below is CORRECT — do not 'fix' it.

preprocessor.comment: kama has no preprocessor: the lexer SILENTLY DROPS `reserved_preprocessor ^[ \t]*#.*` (kama.l), which exists only so `#region`/`#endregion` can drive editor folding. Colouring it like a comment is honest — that is exactly what the compiler does with the line.
preprocessor.name: comment.line.number-sign.kama

asm.comment: `asm_statement : ASM LPAREN STRING_LITERAL RPAREN SEMICOLON` (kama.y) takes a PLAIN string literal, so the body deliberately does NOT include #interp-body: an interpolated `asm("${x}")` does not parse, and a live-looking hole would colour un-compilable code as valid. Must be included BEFORE #keywords — `asm` is a reserved keyword, and TextMate breaks a same-position tie in favour of the EARLIER include, so #keywords would otherwise starve this rule of its `asm` anchor.
asm.name: string.quoted.double.asm.kama

patterns.comment: html"…" tagged string — inject HTML highlighting into the body, keep ${…} holes live
patterns.name: string.quoted.double.tagged.html.kama

patterns.comment: sql"…" tagged string — inject SQL highlighting into the body, keep ${…} holes live
patterns.name: string.quoted.double.tagged.sql.kama

patterns.comment: a generic tag"…" tagged string (stripIndent, user tags) — highlight the tag, keep ${…} holes
patterns.name: string.quoted.double.tagged.kama

patterns.comment: Verbatim `@"…"`: no escapes EXCEPT `quote_esc_seq \"\"` (kama.l), which is a literal quote. The end pattern needs the negative lookahead — TextMate prefers `end` over a content pattern at a tie, so a plain `"` end would terminate the string on the first half of `""` and mis-colour the rest of the line (which it did).
patterns.name: string.quoted.verbatim.kama

escapes.comment: Mirrors kama.l EXACTLY: `simple_esc_seq \\['\"\\0abfnrtv$]` plus `uni_codepoint_esc_seq \\u\{{hex_digit}{1,6}\}`. Everything else after a backslash is NOT an escape — `\e`, `\x41` and `\q` are all rejected by the compiler, and the hex run is bounded at 6 (U+10FFFF), so `\u{1234567}` is invalid too. The catch-all second rule colours those as illegal instead of letting them pass as valid escapes, which is what the old single `\\(u\{…\}|.)` rule did.

patterns.comment: string interpolation hole ${ident.field[index]:spec} — an identifier with .field/[index] accessors and an optional format spec
patterns.name: meta.interpolation.kama

patterns.comment: format specifier :.2 / :0x / :+06 — highlighted as a unit before the accessor rules
patterns.name: keyword.other.format-spec.kama

chars.comment: A `char` is exactly ONE Unicode scalar value. kama.l offers four spellings and no more: `simple_esc_seq_literal` ('\n'), `single_char_literal` ('a'), `uni_codepoint_char_literal` ('\u{1..6 hex}') and `multibyte_char_literal` (one 2-4 byte UTF-8 scalar, 'é'/'😀'). This used to be a quoted SPAN, which accepted `'abc'` and `''` — a multi-codepoint grapheme is a string, not a char, so both are rejected by the compiler and are now coloured illegal. Match rules rather than a span also mean a stray `'` no longer swallows the rest of the line.

patterns.comment: Reached only when neither spelling above matched: `''`, `'abc'`, `'\e'`, `'\u{1234567}'`.
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.char-literal.kama

attributes.comment: `@generate`, `@compileFor(FLAG)`, `@noheap`, `@skip`, `@interrupt`, `@section(...)`, `@align(N)`, `@packed`, `@builtin`, `@vertex`… There was no rule at all, so an attribute was invisible and — worse — one with arguments mis-scoped as a FUNCTION CALL (`compileFor` matched #functions' trailing-`(` lookahead). Anchored on the `@`, which is left of the name, so it wins on position regardless of include order; it is listed before #declarations anyway because `@generate(...) type …` is a legal prefix (kama.y marked_type_declaration).

declarations.comment: ⚠️ MUST be included BEFORE #keywords. TextMate breaks a same-position tie in favour of the earlier include, so with #keywords first this rule was DEAD: `type` matched as a bare keyword, scanning resumed past it, and the contextual kind word — which is an ordinary IDENTIFIER in kama.y, so nothing else can colour it — came back with NO scope at all. Verified with the real tokenizer, not reasoned about; tests/syntax/declarations.kama locks it down. `modifiers_opt` sits between `type` and the kind word (kama.y `marked_type_declaration`), and `type immutable value` / `type abstract resource` / `type extern value` / `type final resource` / `type virtual value` are all in-tree.

keywords.comment: Every row of kama.l's `keywords[]` table must appear in a `\b(…)\b` alternation here or in #types/#constants/#declarations — tools/check-syntax-drift.sh fails the build otherwise. `using` was highlighted and is NOT a keyword: it was retired in favour of `import` (docs/KEYWORDS.md).

patterns.comment: A capitalized word is PROBABLY a type — a regex cannot know. `textDocument/semanticTokens` is the layer that corrects it, because only the resolver can tell a type from a value.
patterns.name: entity.name.type.kama

numbers.comment: Mirrors kama.l exactly; guarded by tools/check-syntax-drift.sh. Three things the earlier rules got wrong: the integer suffix is `u?i(8|16|32|64)`, so it is `42ui32` and there is NO bare `42u32`; kama has NO digit separators, so `1_000` is not a literal; and a float suffix needs a fractional part, so `42f32` is not one either. Each literal splits its digits from its TYPE SUFFIX via captures, so `i32` in `42i32` colors like the `int32` keyword rather than like the digits. Anything else starting with a digit is flagged illegal instead of being coloured as a valid number.

patterns.comment: Based literal `0b<digits>_<base 2..32>` (e.g. 0b1010_2) — must precede the integer rule.
`digits.digits` with an optional exponent, or `digits` with a required one (1e10). A dot needs digits on both sides, so `1.` and `.5` fall through to the illegal rule.
Reached only when every rule above failed: a bad suffix (42u32, 42f32), a digit separator (1_000), or a based literal with no `_<base>` (0b1010).
patterns.name: invalid.illegal.numeric.kama

operators.comment: There were no operator rules at all. Every spelling below is a token in kama.l — note what is NOT here: kama has no `->` (a function is `fn <returnType> name(…)`, C-style, kama.y function_return_type), and bare `:` is deliberately unscoped because in kama it is overwhelmingly the NAMED-ARGUMENT separator (`f(item: x)`), not a ternary arm. `::` covers both qualification and the turbofish `::<T>` (tests/io_streams.kama:44).

functions.comment: Included LAST on purpose: the trailing-`(` lookahead also matches `if (`, `match (`, `asm (` and `@compileFor(`, so every rule that owns one of those words has to be reached first.
